notes: Antarctica is governed through the Antarctic Treaty System rather than as a sovereign country. Treaty-designated ASPAs and ASMAs are not national parks of a country, so no country-level denominator or national-park percentage applies.

KEPA reports the Sharr National Park was declared in 1986 and covers 39,000 ha. The Kosovo-under-UNSCR-1244 statistical annex reports 10,887 km2 for 2001; 390 km2 / 10,887 km2 = 3.5823%. Park operations were suspended in 1999-2002, so this is designated area, not active-management coverage. The 2003 biodiversity assessment gives a later all-category protected-area total; it is not a 2000 all-category observation and must not replace the UNSD field.

The 2001 yearbook lists 54 km2 Biogradska Gora, 390 km2 Durmitor, 64 km2 Lovcen, and 400 km2 Lake of Skadar basin (908 km2 all-surface total). The same yearbook reports the Montenegro part of Lake Skadar at 369.7 km2. Subtracting the full lake area from the Skadar park and summing the other three parks yields an inferred conservative terrestrial lower bound: 54 + 390 + 64 + (400 - 369.7) = 538.3 km2. Divide by FAO FRA 2000 land area of 13,450 km2 for 4.0022%. The park boundary and water/land split are not directly reported; this is a derived inference, not a complete 2001 park inventory.

The Ministry register lists all 25 protected-area designations through 1999 as reefs, channels, thilas, or other marine sites; its first listed terrestrial wetland designation is dated 2004. A terrestrial national-park area and the 2000 terrestrial protected-area share are therefore explicitly derived as zero from the official dated register. This is not a direct UNSD observation.

notes: A Pacific Community (SPC/SOPAC) environmental-vulnerability field report from April 2000 states there were no terrestrial or marine reserves set aside for environmental management or refugia and that environmental legislation was still in draft. This contemporaneous report supports 0% nationally designated terrestrial protected area in 2000 and zero designated national-park area. The 1996 Nauru National Environmental Management Strategy also presents conservation areas as future proposals; the later CBD report says no protected area had been gazetted. This is a reported zero, not a missing value; candidate conservation sites and non-designated land are not counted.

notes: PCBS/EQA reports a 2014 National Spatial Plan total of 51,157 ha of West Bank natural reserves, including East Jerusalem; this is not a 2001 observation and is not a national-parks-only figure. A separate PCBS 2001–2002 release reports 19 natural reserves and about 54 km2 in the West Bank, unchanged from the previous year; this is a distinct approximate natural-reserves observation, not a parks-only value or full Palestinian Territory total. The UN report describes protected-area planning as suspended since 2000. No comparable 2001 national-park aggregate is asserted.

San Marino's later CBD NBSAP reports protected-natural-area planning zones covering 39% of the territory under laws dating to 1992 and 1995, but does not provide a 2001 observation or a national-parks-only area. The 39% figure is not used as a 2001 override.

South Sudan became independent in 2011; in 2001 the territory was part of Sudan. The Sudan government's 2004 Dinder National Park Management Plan, Table 4, lists Southern National Park (established 1939; 2,300,000 ha), Nimule (1945; 41,000 ha), Boma (1986; 2,280,000 ha), Bandingilo (1986; 1,650,000 ha), and Shambe (1985; 62,000 ha) in a Sudan-wide roster. These areas are not reported for a separate South Sudan territory. The 2018 South Sudan CBD strategy uses different areas/classifications and includes proposed changes. Without a documented 2001 territorial partition, consistent park boundaries, and a compatible denominator, do not sum or backcast these candidates into an SSD national-park value.

The country's CBD Sixth National Report says the Obô de Sao Tome and Obô do Principe Natural Parks were established under Laws 6/2006 and 7/2006. This supports zero formally designated national-park area in 2001 only; forest legislation and other conservation categories mean it does not establish zero for all terrestrial protected areas.

The official end-of-2001 park profile lists 18,083 ha of Kenting land, 15,186 ha of Kenting marine area, and land areas of 105,491 ha Yushan, 11,455 ha Yangmingshan, 92,000 ha Taroko, 76,850 ha Sheipa, and 3,780 ha Kinmen. Excluding Kenting's marine row gives 307,659 ha = 3,076.59 km2. The official 2001 land-area denominator is 36,188.04 km2; the derived parks-only land share is 8.5017%. This is not the broader UNSD all-category protected-area metric.
